entry.name: rate~
entry.digest: Time-scale the output of a phasor~
entry.description: The rate~ object accepts an input signal from a phasor~ and time scales it by a multiplier received as a float in its right inlet. Numbers less than 1 create several ramps per phase cycle. Numbers greater than 1 create fewer ramps. This can be useful for implementing a phasor~-synchronized system in MSP.

arguments.name: multiplier
arguments.description: The multiplier value used to scale the output signal.

attributes.name: sync
attributes.digest: Set the sync mode
attributes.description: Sets the sync mode of theobject. The sync mode determines whether or not the"in" will stay in phase with the input signal, and the method used for synchronization. When the output of theobject is "in phase," the input and output signals align precisely at the least common multiple of their periods (i.e., they pass through zero and begin a new cycle at precisely the same time). If the signals are in phase, and a new multiplier value is received, theobject changes the frequency of its output ramp accordingly. However, the change in multiplier values means that the two signals may be out of phase. Theobject handles this situation in one of three different ways, depending on the sync mode

choices.digest: Set the cycle mode for sync
choices.label: The argumentsorset the cycle mode of theobject. In cycle mode, theobject does not change the phase of its output until the end of the current cycle. When the input ramp reaches its peak and starts over from zero, theobject immediately restarts the output ramp, causing a discontinuity in the output signal, and immediate phase synchronization.

choices.digest: Set the lock mode for sync
choices.label: The argumentsorset the lock mode of theobject. In sync lock mode, theobject performs synchronization whenever a new multiplier is received. Theobject immediately calculates the proper ramp position which corresponds to being "in phase" with the new multiplier value, and jumps to that position.

The argumentsordisables the sync mode of theobject (the default mode). In this modenever responds to phase differences; when a new multiplier is received, theobject adjusts the speed of its output ramps and they continue without interruption. Since this mode never introduces a discontinuous jump in the ramp signal, it may be useful if phase is unimportant.

messages.name: float
messages.digest: In left inlet: Sets the phase value for theobject's signal output
messages.description: In left inlet: Sets the phase value for theobject's signal output.In right inlet: The signal multiplier value used to scale thesignal input. Float values less than 1.0 create several ramps per phase cycle. Numbers greater than 1.0 create fewer ramps. This can be useful for synchronizing multiple processes to a single referenceobject, preserving their ratio relationships.

messages.name: goto
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by a float, causes theobject to jump immediately to the specified value. An optional second argument may be used to specify the time at which to jump to the value (e.g.,will output a value of 1.0 at the halfway point of theobject's input signal ramp).

messages.name: int
messages.description: In left inlet: Sets the phase value for theobject's signal output.In right inlet: The signal multiplier value used to scale thesignal input. Integer values greater than 1 create fewer ramps. This can be useful for synchronizing multiple processes to a single referenceobject, preserving their ratio relationships.
